w:r.w:t: Estimating Traffic States on Urban Motorways
A macroscopic approach with loop detectors and floating cars
Thesis submitted for the degree of Master of Science

Reliable estimates of traffic density are the basis of ramp metering, travel-time information and incident detection. This thesis combines the first-order kinematic wave model with a Kalman filter that fuses loop detector counts and floating-car speeds. On a 12 km stretch of the Rotterdam ring road the filter reduces the density error by 31% compared with detector data alone, and it locates stop-and-go waves within one cell of their true position.
I thank my supervisors for their patience, and the road authority for the detector data.

Congestion on urban motorways costs time, fuel and reliability. Traffic managers react to it with ramp metering
, variable speed limits and travel-time information, and every one of these measures needs to know the current
: how many vehicles there are on each stretch of road, and how fast they move.
count vehicles at fixed points, typically every 500 m. Between them the state is unknown. Floating cars
, vehicles that report their position and speed, cover the gaps but only sample a few percent of the traffic. Neither source alone gives the full picture.
